title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
summary: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

title: First constraints on axion-like particles with SPHEREx data
summary: We present the first search for axion-like particle dark matter using SPHEREx data. We perform a conservative analysis on the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx data and derive new limits on the mass range $0.496 < m_a < 3.32\,\mathrm{eV}$ that are competitive with the literature. Our tightest limit on the coupling relative to those previously published is $g_{aγγ} < 2.10 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a = 0.606\,\mathrm{eV}$, with a median limit of $g_{aγγ} < 4.16 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Cast as model-independent limits on the lifetime of the dark matter particle, the median limit is $τ> 6.5 \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{s}$. We are also able to detect several expected emission features at high significance, such as atmospheric He I and the 3.3 $μ$m PAH feature. We calculate the Cramér-Rao bound and compare to sensitivity forecasts, finding that our limits could be improved by more than an order of magnitude with solely methodological improvements.

title: Construction of the $f_4$ meson family
summary: Motivated by the experimental observations of $f_4(2050)$ and $f_4(2300)$ and the establishment of $a_4$ family, we investigate the $f_4$ family by combining the mass spectrum under the modified Godfrey--Isgur model with two-body strong-decay calculations in the quark-pair-creation model. The common pair-creation strength is fixed by the measured total width of $f_4(2050)$. The mass spectrum analysis and decay information both favor the nonstrange $2\,{}^3F_4$ assignment for $f_4(2300)$. The largely strange $2F$ partner is predicted at $2453$ MeV with a total width of $216$ MeV, decaying mainly into $K^*\bar K^*(1410)$ and $K^*\bar K^*$. Predictions are also given for the $3F$, $4F$, $1H$, and $2H$ flavor pairs. At the adopted mixing angles, the $H$-wave states are more than twice as broad as nearby $F$-wave states of the same flavor. The results of this work may serve as useful guidance for future experimental studies.

title: Shot noise, aperture and resolution in Fourier measurements of disc lopsidedness: TNG50-1 and TNG100-1 analysed with TNGGalaxyLab
comment: 1 pages, 10 figures. The TNGGalaxyLab Python pipeline and catalogues are publicly available
summary: We present TNGGalaxyLab, an open-source Python pipeline for particle-based Fourier decomposition of the stellar surface density of simulated disc galaxies. It measures m = 1-4 amplitude and phase profiles in the Rix and Zaritsky (1995) normalisation, handles IllustrisTNG snapshot conventions, and recovers injected amplitudes in synthetic discs to better than 2 per cent at N = 5 x 10^5. Fourier amplitudes are positive-definite, so Poisson noise biases them upwards by an amount that grows as the particle number falls. We measure a per-galaxy noise floor by randomising particle azimuths and define a noise-corrected amplitude A1,corr. Downsampling TNG50-1 discs to the TNG100-1 particle mass inflates the uncorrected A1 by 40-60 per cent, while A1,corr is recovered to within approximately 10 per cent. We then process all central galaxies with 3.16 x 10^9 < M*/Msun < 10^11 in TNG50-1 (915) and TNG100-1 (6717) with identical settings in the [1.5, 2.5] Rd aperture. Removing the bootstrap and shot-noise biases lowers the TNG100/TNG50 ratio of median A1 from 2.3 to 1.6. At fixed stellar mass, kinematically selected TNG100-1 discs remain 1.5-1.9 times more lopsided after correction; this excess persists whether the aperture is defined in Rd or in kpc, is not explained by kappa_rot or D/T, and is largest at 3.5-6 kpc. TNG50-1 is statistically consistent with the mass-matched S4G sample of Zaritsky et al. (2013); TNG100-1 is not. The low A1 reported for TNG100 by Lokas (2022) cannot be read as a resolution deficit, since with matched measurements TNG100-1 is more lopsided than TNG50-1. Code and catalogues are public.

title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
summary: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/ω$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

title: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
summary: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.

title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 33 pages, 22 figures, 5 tables
summary: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.

title: Three Dimensional Structure of Pion with One Dynamical Gluon in the Light-Cone Quark Model
summary: We study the three-dimensional structure of the pion beyond the leading Fock state by including a dynamical gluon, $|π\rangle=|q\bar q\rangle+|q\bar q g\rangle$. Within the light-cone quark model, we calculate the pion GPDs, TMDs, and PDFs from light-front wave function overlaps, using a modified Brodsky--Huang--Lepage wave function with the Melosh--Wigner rotation for the valence sector and the light-front quark--gluon vertex for the $q\bar q g$ sector. The quark-number and momentum sum rules are satisfied without additional constraints. We further obtain the electromagnetic form factor and the mass decomposition. After NLO evolution, we compare the PDFs with pion-induced Drell--Yan, $J/ψ$, $Υ$, and HERA leading-neutron $F_2^π$ data. The $q\bar q g$ sector contributes little to Drell--Yan but becomes important for gluon-sensitive observables such as $J/ψ$ production and the pion structure function at small $x$.

title: Tracing the Epoch of Reionization through extreme emission line galaxies around Cosmic Noon
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A (06 Nov 2026)
summary: Star-forming galaxies at z>6 are thought to be the main drivers of cosmic reionization, but their faintness makes detailed study challenging even with JWST. Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems with intense nebular emission and are potential lower-redshift analogues of this population. We aim to assemble and characterize a statistically significant sample of EELGs in the CANDELS/EGS field around cosmic noon, and to assess their validity as analogues of the galaxies that drove reionization. We select EELG candidates from CANDELS photometry with a J-band color-excess criterion that identifies both H$β$+[OIII] and H$α$ emitters. Physical properties are taken from CANDELS data products, and the selection is validated with MMT/MMIRS, Keck/MOSFIRE, HST/WFC3 and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, complemented by our own GTC/OSIRIS+ program. We identify 102 H$β$+[OIII] emitters at $z\sim1.7$ and 127 H$α$ emitters at $z\sim1.0$. They are compact ($\sim$1.6 kpc), low-mass ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim8$) and strongly star-forming (sSFR $\sim10^{-8}$ yr$^{-1}$). Estimated purities of $84.3\pm1.5$\% (H$β$+[OIII]) and $76.8\pm2.0$\% (H$α$) agree with spectroscopic confirmation rates (85\% and 63\%), with no evidence of significant AGN contamination. A joint Bayesian fit, corrected for completeness via a truncated likelihood, yields $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) = (6.71\pm0.16) + (3.31\pm0.46)\log(1+z)$, suggesting an evolution in the characteristic mass of the sample with cosmic time. We spectroscopically confirm a highly pure, AGN-free sample of cosmic-noon EELGs. While their mass scale evolves with redshift, their properties consistently match those of z>5 JWST extreme emitters, supporting them as intermediate-redshift analogues.

title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
summary: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.

title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

title: Helicity Decay to Baryons: The Cosmological Evolution of $L_μ-L_τ$ Gauge Fields and Baryogenesis
summary: We study baryogenesis from the post-inflationary decay of helical U(1)$_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge fields generated during axion inflation. Assuming that Schwinger pair production is suppressed during inflation, a large helicity-to-entropy ratio $η_H$ can be generated while keeping the initial lepton asymmetry just after inflation negligible. After reheating, the dissipation of magnetic helicity sources a lepton asymmetry through the chiral anomaly, which is partially converted into a baryon asymmetry by electroweak sphaleron processes. We find that there are parameter spaces where the observed baryon asymmetry can be generated in both the turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes of the U(1)$_{L_μ-L_τ}$ magnetic field evolution. The baryon asymmetry generation in the turbulent regime is, however, dominated by the pre-turbulent nearly frozen regime. We further find that the requirement of successful baryogenesis imposes stronger constraints on the inflationary Hubble parameter and the helicity density generated during axion inflation than the requirement for the gauge-field energy not to backreact on the inflaton dynamics.

title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Through Exponential Production Mechanism
summary: Exponential production of dark matter has been introduced recently as one of the alternatives to the widely studied thermal production of dark matter scenarios. This non-thermal production mechanism leads to the exponential growth in the abundance of the dark matter ($χ$) through its scatterings with the bath particle ($ξ$), viz. $χ+ ξ\to χ+ χ$. In our framework, we consider a scalar dark matter $χ$ charged under $Z_3$ symmetry and bath particle $ξ$ to be standard model singlet and determine the maximum mass of the dark matter using the criteria of perturbativity. We find that dark matter has an upper mass around the ballpark of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV for the cases when the bath particle mass is similar to the dark matter mass. The computations are largely performed with minimal model dependence and will hold in any scenario where the renormalizable couplings driving the exponential growth effectively reduce to $χ^3ξ$ interactions. Thus, in exponential production of dark matter, we have a possibility of an ultra-heavy dark matter with large couplings, making the scenario phenomenologically interesting. Later, we extend the simplified dark matter model to a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model where the $Z_3$ symmetry is obtained as a residual unbroken subgroup of a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, providing a natural connection with the neutrino sector.

title: A Statistical Analysis of Lopsidedness in Disk Galaxies
summary: We present a statistical analysis of Fourier lopsidedness in disk galaxies based on a deduplicated compilation of 606 unique objects: 442 have a measured m = 1 amplitude (A1), and 302 of these also have a measured m = 2 amplitude (A2), with no entry carrying A2 alone. The sample is a factor of approximately 3 larger than earlier homogeneous A1-A2 datasets. Our main results are: (i) Both A1 and A2 follow log-normal distributions (KS D = 0.046 and 0.048) which are strongly preferred over Rayleigh or exponential forms, pointing to a multiplicative amplification process rather than random-phase superposition. (ii) The m = 1 and m = 2 modes are correlated as A2 = 0.29 A1 + 0.11 (Spearman rho = 0.501, p less than 10^-19). (iii) A1 rises monotonically with morphological T-type from approximately 0.07 in E/S0 to approximately 0.37 in Sm/Im galaxies (Kendall tau = 0.234, p approximately 10^-12). (iv) A1 anti-correlates with gas rotation velocity (Spearman rho = -0.432) and, in a stellar-mass cross-matched subsample of 246 galaxies with independent stellar-mass estimates, with stellar mass (rho = -0.395). The weaker lopsidedness of massive, fast-rotating disks indicates that the observed m = 1 amplitude is regulated by internal dynamics rather than set by tidal perturbations alone. (v) The TNG50-1 simulation, analysed through the TNGGalaxyLab Fourier pipeline, reproduces the observed A1-stellar-mass anti-correlation with a nearly identical Spearman coefficient, although its median A1 is approximately 1.4 times lower, an offset consistent with the heterogeneous target selection of the observational compilation.

title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
summary: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.

title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $Λ$CDM
summary: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $ΛCDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $ΛCDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $ΛCDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $γ$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
summary: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_χ/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_χ\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_χ\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

title: Strong decays of $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$ and $ψ(4160)$ in four relativistic wave-function representations
summary: Strong decays provide a direct test of the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions. We study the OZI-allowed hadronic decays of the vector charmonia $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$ and $ψ(4160)$ within the Salpeter equation, using four relativistic wave-function representations $\varphi_1$--$\varphi_4$ that differ in the $S$-, $P$- and $D$-wave components they retain independently, and the revised ${}^3P_0$ model. The quark-pair creation strength is fixed once, by reproducing the measured $ψ(3770)\to D\bar D$ width, and is not readjusted afterwards, so that the results for the two higher states are parameter-free predictions. The representation $\varphi_2$ predicts $94^{+34}_{-23}$~MeV for $ψ(4040)$ and $100^{+23}_{-20}$~MeV for $ψ(4160)$, in agreement with the measured $84.5\pm12.3$ and $69\pm10$~MeV, and it is the only one whose predicted width ratios are compatible with the data. By contrast, $\varphi_1$ overshoots $ψ(4040)$ by $2.5σ$, $\varphi_3$ gives the largest widths and is disfavoured at the $5σ$ level, and $\varphi_4$, which has no independent $S$-wave component, underestimates $ψ(3770)$ by about $2σ$ and cannot be applied to final states containing vector mesons. These results show that a successful representation must contain independent $S$, $P$ and $D$ components, the $P$-wave terms providing the dominant relativistic correction, while the nodal structure of the wave functions accounts for the large uncertainties of the predictions. The mixing angles extracted from $\varphi_2$, $7.92^{\circ}$, $25.8^{\circ}$ and $26.3^{\circ}$, agree with the values obtained in coupled-channel models.

title: Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies
summary: Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.

title: Bions and infrared renormalons in Kähler sigma models with $U(1)$ isotropy
summary: We study semiclassical bion contributions to the vacuum energy of Kähler sigma models with two-dimensional target spaces on $\mathbb{R} \times S^1$ with twisted boundary conditions. This is first illustrated in the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model, where explicit real and complex bion solutions are constructed in a manner analogous to that used in its quantum-mechanical reduction [1]. Evaluating the bosonic and fermionic fluctuations at one loop, we obtain the effective action with both the coupling constant and the elongation parameter properly renormalized. Integration over the bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles then gives the leading nonperturbative contribution, which the real and complex bion contributions cancel at the supersymmetric point, while the first imaginary ambiguity appears when deviating from the supersymmetric point. Requiring its cancellation against the perturbative ambiguity allows us to infer the corresponding infrared-renormalon pole. This is an explicit example generalizing the resurgent structure of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model in [2] from one coupling to two renormalized parameters. The calculation further extends to Kähler targets of one complex dimension with a $U(1)$ symmetry. At leading dilute one-loop order, the target dependence enters through the moment-map difference and the metric normalizations at the two fixed points. The ambiguity structure and infrared scaling of the bion weight are common to these targets, while the inferred pole position depends on the target metric.

title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
summary: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

title: The $χ_{c1}(3872)$ Multiplet in the Diabatic Dynamical Diquark Model
summary: We apply a minimal form of the diabatic dynamical diquark model, which uses only dimeson thresholds augmented by constraints obtained from heavy-quark spin symmetry, to the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum. We find that this model is insufficient to simultaneously reproduce the experimentally established states \(χ_{c1}(3872)\), \(T_{c\bar c1}(3900)\), and \(T_{c\bar c1}(4020)\). We therefore extend the model to its complete form, by restoring the spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic dynamical diquark model into the full diabatic potential. Aligning the resulting framework to these three states allows the remaining members of the \(Σ_g^+(1S)\) multiplet to be predicted through coupled-channel scattering simulations. The resulting resonance or bound state locations lie within approximately \(10~\mathrm{MeV}\) of the corresponding pure adiabatic mass eigenvalue predictions in all cases, indicating that the adiabatic fine-structure pattern survives the inclusion of explicit dimeson channels. We also discuss possible experimental counterparts for the unconfirmed multiplet members.

title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, submitted to ApjL. Comments welcome
summary: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II
summary: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlevé II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.

title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
summary: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

title: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
comment: 27 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables, prepared for submission to JCAP
summary: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.

title: Resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ interference in $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at NLO: Hard matching and radiative charm-loop jet function for $m_c \to 0$
comment: 32 pages, 11 figures. Analytic results for the master integrals provided as an ancillary Mathematica notebook
summary: We study next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ arising from the interference of the current-current operator $Q_1^q$ and the electromagnetic dipole operator $Q_{7γ}$. This contribution is among the main sources of theoretical uncertainty in Standard Model predictions for the decay rate. Using a factorisation theorem in soft-collinear effective theory for the kinematic endpoint region, $m_b-2E_γ=\mathcal{O}(Λ_{\rm QCD})$, we determine all previously unknown perturbative ingredients at NLO in the limit of a vanishing charm-quark mass, $m_c\to0$. Specifically, we compute the $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients, derive their renormalisation-group equations, and obtain accurate analytic approximations to their solutions by retaining the first two terms in a $1/N_c$ expansion. Our second main result is the two-loop correction to the radiative charm-loop jet function, including its full dependence on the collinear momentum fraction. Combining these results with the known $\mathcal{O}(α_s)$ correction to the quark jet function and the one-loop renormalisation of the subleading shape function $g_{17}$, previously computed by some of us, we provide the first complete NLO description of this resolved contribution in the massless-charm limit. This leaves the $m_c$ dependence of the radiative charm-loop jet function as the remaining ingredient for a phenomenological analysis within renormalisation-group-improved perturbation theory.

title: Spacetime contactability in Galactic civilization networks: Contact counts and percolation
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables, submitted to Acta Astronautica
summary: The number of Galactic civilizations does not determine whether they are in contact. Allowing civilizations to appear at different times separates listening, audibility, mutual-listening, and relay networks, with a distinct reply-closing condition requiring a return signal within the sender's lifetime. For each network we derive the contact counts and estimate the connectivity threshold in a uniform population, then apply the results to a structured Galactic disc, separating the detection range $d_{\rm max}$ from the light horizon $cL$ through $χ=d_{\rm max}/cL$. The contactability is $η=πn d_{\rm max}^{2}$, where $n$ is the active civilization surface density. Averaged over civilization appearances, the lifetime listening count is $2η$ for all $χ$ and, at fixed detection range, for any lifetime distribution. Audibility and mutual-listening counts sum to $4η$, but connectivity depends on threshold behavior rather than counts alone. As $χ\rightarrow0$, the listening threshold decreases from the coeval value $4.51$ to $1.32\pm0.01$. Assuming an ideal complete survey, our own non-detection gives the reference bound $η(R_0)\le2.75$ at the Sun's Galactocentric radius. This benchmark lies above the listening, audibility and relay thresholds throughout the range studied. Unlike the coeval model, the spacetime model can satisfy both this benchmark and a local connectivity criterion, moving the local-contact frontier outward by $3.2$ kpc. Under the same benchmark, civilizations hear at most $5.5$ others on average, while the mean reply-closing count falls below unity for $χ\gtrsim1$. Contact may therefore be common even when completed replies remain rare.

title: Geometry of Gauge-invariant Quantum Fields
comment: 11 pages, submitted to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics Valladolid (Spain), 13-17 July 2026
summary: Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the Stückelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.

title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
summary: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$Δ$ contact interactions with an explicit $Δ$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
summary: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $Δ$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $Δ$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $ΔΔ$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $Λ^2/κ_{ΔΔ}^2$, where $κ_{ΔΔ}=\sqrt{2M_Δ(M_Δ-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$Δ$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $Δ$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$ΔΔ$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $κ_{ΔΔ}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $ΔΔ$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.

title: Aster: A Flexible and Robust Collection of Numerical Tools for N-Body Problems
summary: The Aster library is an open-source collection of numerical tools designed for large-scale gravitational N-body simulations. Aster provides a flexible environment to its users, enabling it to be used in the analysis of a broad range of astrophysical problems. The library implements efficient force calculation algorithms, including a spatial tree solver optimized with coordinate-dependent identifiers, which has been fine-tuned for both CPU and GPU architectures. Despite its high degree of modularity, many parts of the library have been optimized with SIMD instructions, heavy parallelization, and support on dedicated hardware. Aster also offers a wide variety of numerical symplectic integrators, such as SABA (from first to tenth order), the classic leapfrog algorithm, and the more advanced Wisdom-Holman (WH) integrator, while also providing a vast collection of mathematical tools, e.g., post-newtonian expansions (1PN, 2PN, 2.5PN), data collection and graphing systems, a built-in renderer, and presets for faster instantiation of large amounts of bodies. In this work we will discuss in depth the details of each module as well as the results of several performance- and accuracy-related tests, probing the library's capabilities in different physical applications.

title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
summary: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.

title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
comment: 38 pages, 4 figures. Invited topical review, published in Reports on Progress in Physics
summary: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.

title: Extracting Published Discussions of 13,616 Galaxies with Language Models
comment: Accepted to the Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for Scientific Publications (WASP) 2026
summary: Astronomers often have difficulty determining whether an object, such as a star or galaxy of interest, has been discussed in the literature. Existing tools enable object identification and linking in papers but do not record whether an object was genuinely discussed in a paper or just appears in a table or catalog. We address this by using language model agents to identify galaxies discussed in more than two sentences across a corpus of 156,006 arXiv astro-ph papers and extract those discussions. We extract 44,332 discussions of individual galaxies containing 85,314 quotes from 18,641 papers. With sky coordinates for 98.2% of discussions, we group them into 13,616 galaxies. We bring these results together into GalaxyWiki, where users can find literature discussing galaxies, read what was said about them, and follow links to the source papers. The code, dataset, and webpage are available at https://github.com/NolanKoblischke/galaxywiki-paper

title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum field theory
summary: How does a scalar field oscillating about a metastable minimum decay? For a coherent state with $\langle q(t) \rangle = a \cos mt$ we find two results. When $mR \ll 1$, with $m$ the mass and $R$ the bubble radius, the decay at time $t$ is a Coleman bubble in the frozen potential $U_t(η) = U(\langle q \rangle +η)-U(\langle q \rangle)-U'(\langle q \rangle)η$, for any amplitude. At small amplitude but any $mR$, $B(t)=B_0 - a \mathcal{M} \cos mt+O(a^2)$, with $\mathcal{M}$ set by the tail of the vacuum bounce; for a thin wall $\mathcal{M} \propto e^{mR}$, so exponentially small oscillations change the rate significantly. Both results follow from a Euclidean source construction. The same method computes the tunneling rate of a field slowly rolling in one direction and metastable in another.

title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
summary: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $Γ$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $Γ= 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
comment: 24 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Companion paper (HEART model): arXiv:2611.11570
summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form. It supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems, with the shrinkage of the Pomeron in its transfer dependence. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The review follows the cascade description through its predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions) assembles these pieces into an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) defines it and tests it against the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, the local balance of strangeness in associated production, and forward resonance signals with their mass tails.

title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
summary: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
summary: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
summary: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. We reanalyze all of these bounds for the couplings to photons, electrons and nucleons. Space-based tests are weakened by several orders of magnitude, whereas the terrestrial tests are suppressed far more strongly and lose their sensitivity at low masses. As a result, for each coupling, $f$-dependent windows in the parameter space open up. For a coupling to nucleons a window persists at large couplings even for $f\sim 100 \,\rm{GeV}$. In particular, no current experiment constrains couplings between the naive limit and the stellar-cooling bound in a window of masses above $\text{few}\times 10^{-12}\,$eV, a range of more than ten orders of magnitude in coupling. This presents a unique opportunity for a ground-space clock comparison test to probe uncharted territory.

title: ExoPlanetLab: Bayesian orbit fitting of Gaia-DR4 epoch astrometry, radial velocities and relative astrometry
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/hobbsSe/ExoPlanetLab, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24101622
summary: Gaia Data Release 4 (DR4) provides epoch astrometry from which thousands of giant planets and many substellar and stellar companions can be characterised. We present ExoPlanetLab, an open-source package for Bayesian orbit inference from Gaia epoch astrometry, radial velocities (RVs) and relative astrometry, validated on simulated and real data. The model orbit is compared with the epoch residuals after removing the part absorbed by the single-star fit. A Student-t likelihood describes heavy-tailed data. A robust Keplerian periodogram with bootstrap false-alarm probabilities gives starting values for a joint fit. Five samplers are available: tempered ensemble MCMC, two nested samplers and two reversible-jump samplers. Evidences for a fixed number of companions select that number. Acceleration and scan-angle models test whether an orbit is warranted. The samplers agree within 0.1 sigma on a simulated two-planet system. In 180 injections all fits converge, and all signals with signal-to-noise ratio S >= 10 are detected. The posteriors show no significant bias, but the period coverage is below nominal: 90% of the true periods lie within their 95% credible intervals. None of 30 companion-free data sets gives a false detection. On DR4 pre-release data the orbit of Gaia BH3 is recovered within 1.4 sigma of published solutions. The Student-t model brings the astrometric period and eccentricity of HD 114762 onto its RV orbit. Eight simulated relative positions narrow the period's credible interval to 0.27 of its width, and Octofitter agrees within 0.2 sigma on the same data. The code is validated for single sources with DR4-like epoch astrometry, with or without RVs. Relative astrometry is tested on simulated data only. The main limits are an uncorrelated noise model and the computing cost, which grows linearly with the number of measurements and steeply with the number of companions.

title: Generalizations of Courant brackets in the T-dual description of a weakly curved string background
summary: When T-duality is realized as a canonical transformation, the standard Courant bracket is T-dual invariant, while the $B$- and $θ$-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged. We determine how these relations are modified for a closed bosonic string moving in a weakly curved background with a constant metric and a Kalb-Ramond field with linear coordinate dependence. We work to first order in its constant field strength. The T-dual background fields depend on a line integral of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields, making the dual description nonlocal. We construct generalized charges whose parameters depend on this line integral and calculate their Poisson bracket algebra using the T-duality transformation laws and the canonical brackets of the initial theory. The resulting algebra yields a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid. We establish an explicit isomorphism with the standard Courant algebroid by transporting the bracket, pairing, and anchor. Applying $B$- and $θ$-shifts to the dual currents, we obtain weakly curved generalizations of the respective twisted Courant brackets. We show that these brackets provide the T-dual realizations of the initial $θ$- and $B$-twisted Courant brackets, respectively, and identify the corresponding Courant algebroid isomorphisms.

title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
summary: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.

title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading
comment: 64 pages, comments and references are welcome;
summary: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.

title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
summary: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

title: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
summary:
We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $η=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $ε$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $σ=0.076$ and $ν_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_σ=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_σ$, we obtain $η=-0.795(21)$ and $ω=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$.
  For the complex Yang-Lee fixed point, convergence of the field expansion depends crucially on its reference point. Expansions about $φ=0$ fail to converge with the smooth regulator used here, whereas expansions about the running imaginary field value at which the mass vanishes converge down to $d=1.3$. This representation preserves the exact relation between the thermal eigenvalue and the field dimension, and hence the hyperscaling identity $θ_h+θ_t=d$, at every field-truncation order. We trace the large violations reported in earlier works to the omission of the expansion-point motion when linearizing the flow, rather than to the truncation itself.

title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
summary: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
summary: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, Code and rule catalogs available at https://github.com/XiaoMing-lei/MassiveAmplitudeReduction
summary: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.

title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
summary: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
summary: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(φ^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.

title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
comment: 23 pages including 7 figures (7 png files). Comments are welcome!
summary: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-ΓH^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $Γ={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $σ\equivΓ/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $σ$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2σ/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(σm_ν^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $Γ=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$Γ$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $Γ\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($σ\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI. Finally, we identify metastable resonances in the spectrum.
